name: Alpine apk (digits, letter, suffixes, ~hash, -rN)
prerelease: _alpha, _beta, _pre, _rc (+ optional number): strictly below the bare version; ladder alpha < beta < pre < rc < release.
buildMetadata: None. ~<hex> commit hash (apk-tools 3 only) participates in ordering and sorts above the bare version.
postRelease: _p<N>, _cvs, _svn, _git, _hg suffixes and a single trailing letter sort above the bare version (cvs < svn < git < hg < p < letter).
yankedDeprecated: No in-band flag. Packages are deleted from a repository branch (edge, vX.Y); secdb lists fixed versions as pkgver-rN.
stableRule: Version must pass apk_version_validate (otherwise unparseable). It is UNSTABLE iff it contains _alpha, _beta, _pre or _rc (regex _(alpha|beta|pre|rc)\d*), a snapshot suffix _(git|hg|cvs|svn)\d*, or a ~<hex> commit marker. -rN (pkgrel, including security bumps), _p<N>, and a trailing letter are STABLE.

semverEquivalents.buildMetadata: none (~hash is the nearest, but ordered)

conventions: -rN is pkgrel (APKBUILD first release is 0); 1.0 < 1.0-r0 < 1.0-r1 in C apk-tools.
A numeric component with a leading zero switches to raw string comparison (1.01 < 1.1, 1.0 < 1.00).
Suffix ladder: alpha < beta < pre < rc < (none) < cvs < svn < git < hg < p.
Suffixes may chain (1.1.3_pre_p2, 1.0_rc1_git20240101-r3).
Snapshot pkgver convention <last-release>_git<YYYYMMDD>.
Release branches (edge, testing, v3.xx) are channels, not version syntax.
knownGaps: apk-tools 2.14.x differs: no ~hash and a different leading-zero path; which Alpine release ships which apk-tools was not verified.
Compare tokenises invalid input up to the bad token; callers must validate first.
Alpaquita, BellSoft Hardened Containers and MinimOS are mapped here by assumption.

name: Android OSV version (<branch>[L][-qprN][-next]:<SPL>)
prerelease: No documented syntax. The -next suffix on a branch (13-next) is inferred to be an unreleased development track.
buildMetadata: None in OSV strings; AOSP build IDs (PVBB.YYMMDD.bbb[.Cn]) are a separate identifier kind.
postRelease: Security patch level after the colon (:YYYY-MM-DD) is the fix granularity within a branch; -qprN and L are later platform releases within a major.
yankedDeprecated: None in the version string. Branches reach end of life; apps are superseded by a higher versionCode, which can never be reused on Google Play.
stableRule: Version must match ^\d+(\.\d+)?L?(-qpr\d+)?(-next)?(:\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}|:0)?$ (else unparseable: build IDs, AOSP tags, three-component marketing versions). UNSTABLE iff it ends the branch part with -next; bare branches, L, -qprN and any :SPL are STABLE.
conventions: OSV composite <branch>:<SPL>: introduced '<branch>:0', fixed '<branch>:<SPL>', versions list holds the bare branch.
12L is Android 12.1 (API 32); 16-qprN are quarterly platform releases (API 36.N in the build table).
API level is a single integer that cannot be derived from the marketing version; the manifest cannot express minor API levels.
App versionCode is a monotonically increasing positive integer (max 2100000000); versionName is display-only.
Kernel advisories use package name :linux_kernel:<SoC vendor>.
knownGaps: No reference comparator exists; the order is derived from OSV data and Android docs.
The meaning of -next is inferred, not documented.
SPL -01/-05/-06 semantics are not defined on the bulletin overview page.
Build-ID and AOSP-tag ordering is only meaningful within a platform branch and is not implemented.

name: Arch pacman/libalpm (epoch:pkgver-pkgrel)
prerelease: No syntax. A trailing alpha attached directly to a number (1.0rc1) sorts below 1.0 by the trailing-alpha rule; with any separator (1.0_rc1, 1.0.rc1, 1.0~rc1) it sorts ABOVE 1.0.
buildMetadata: None. '+' and '~' are plain separators.
epoch: epoch= in PKGBUILD, epoch: prefix, positive integer default 0, dominates.
postRelease: Extra segment (1.0.1, 1.0.a) sorts above the base.
yankedDeprecated: No in-band flag. Package removed from the sync repo; old builds in the Arch Linux Archive; AUR packages can be deleted or orphaned.
stableRule: No version syntax distinguishes stable, so classify by convention on pkgver (pkgrel and epoch removed): UNSTABLE iff it has a delimited pre-release word (alpha|beta|rc|pre|preview|prerelease|milestone|candidate)\d*, a VCS form (r\d+\.[0-9a-f]{7,}, \.r\d+\.g[0-9a-f]{7,}, \+r\d+\+g[0-9a-f]{7,}, (git|svn|hg|bzr|cvs|darcs) + digits/hex), or a dev/nightly/snapshot word. pkgrel bumps (-2, -1.1), epochs, date versions and single patch letters (1.1.1k) are STABLE.
conventions: pkgver forbids hyphen, colon, slash, whitespace; upstream 1.0-rc1 must be respelled and the spelling changes ordering.
pkgrel is N or N.M; compared only when both versions have one (1.5 == 1.5-1).
VCS packages carry -git/-svn/-hg/-bzr/-cvs/-darcs in the package NAME and generate pkgver via git describe | sed or r<count>.<sha>.
Separator-run length differs => shorter run is older (1.0..1 > 1.0.1).
Repositories (core, extra, *-testing, *-staging) are channels, not version syntax.
knownGaps: Pre-release and snapshot classification is purely heuristic.
libalpm vercmp is rpm 4.8.1-derived: do not reuse the rpm scheme (no ~ or ^).
Arch packaging-guideline text on pre-release spelling was not retrieved.
Manjaro/CachyOS/EndeavourOS rebuild markers not verified.

name: Bitnami X.Y.Z[-revision] (revision-aware SemVer)
prerelease: Not supported as SemVer pre-release: the '-' slot is a REVISION, so 1.0.0-rc1 sorts ABOVE 1.0.0. Named pre-releases are detected by word only.
buildMetadata: +meta is ignored for ordering (1.0.0+a == 1.0.0+b).
postRelease: The revision itself: 2.4.58 < 2.4.58-1 < 2.4.58-2 < 2.4.59; compared as SemVer pre-release identifiers (numeric before alphanumeric, lexical for alphanumerics).
yankedDeprecated: No flag in the version. Old images moved to the bitnamilegacy namespace (no longer updated); rolling tags move on rebuild, immutable tags are fixed.
stableRule: Version must be exactly three numeric components plus optional -revision and +meta (SemVer regex without leading zeros), else unparseable. The revision slot is a REBUILD counter: -N, -rN and -<distro>-<release>-rN (7.2.4-debian-12-r5) are STABLE. UNSTABLE iff the revision part contains a delimited pre-release word (alpha|beta|rc|pre|preview|prerelease|milestone|candidate)\d*, nightly, dev|devel|snapshot|canary, or a VCS word.

unstableMarkers.syntax: delimited alpha|beta|rc|pre words in the revision part
words dev|devel|snapshot|canary in the revision part
word nightly in the revision part
git|svn|hg|bzr|cvs + digits/hex in the revision part

semverEquivalents.prerelease: none (the '-' slot is a post-release revision)

conventions: A plain SemVer comparer ranks 2.4.58-1 below 2.4.58 (real Trivy false positive); Bitnami's comparer ranks any revision above none.
Container tags: rolling 6.4.3 vs immutable 6.4.3-debian-12-r10; rN increments per rebuild and resets to r0 when the base OS changes (debian-11-r4 -> debian-12-r0).
Revision r5 vs r10 in a container tag is ONE alphanumeric identifier and compares lexically (r5 > r10).
Two- or four-component versions are invalid for the comparer.
Helm chart versions are the chart's own SemVer, independent of appVersion.
knownGaps: No official Bitnami document defines the grammar; sources are maintainer statements in the Trivy thread, tag docs via summary, and the go-version code.
Sampled OSV Bitnami data (redis, 50 advisories) used plain SemVer ranges without revisions.
Legacy-namespace move seen only via search summary and Docker Hub listing.

name: Debian dpkg (epoch:upstream-revision)
prerelease: Tilde: 1.0~rc1 sorts before 1.0 (and 1.0~~ < 1.0~~a < 1.0~ < 1.0). A bare 1.0rc1 is NOT ordered as a pre-release: it sorts after 1.0.
buildMetadata: None. +b1 (binNMU), +dfsg, +git2024... are ordinary characters and take part in ordering ('+' sorts after end of string).
epoch: Integer before the first colon, default 0, dominates everything (2:0.1 > 1:9.9).
postRelease: Any +suffix on upstream or revision (+b1, +nmu1, +deb12u1, +really2.2, +dfsg) sorts above the bare version.
yankedDeprecated: No in-band flag. Removal from a suite by ftpmaster (archive); fixed status lives in the Debian Security Tracker; history in snapshot.debian.org.
stableRule: A version is STABLE unless, after deleting the stable tilde tokens ~bpo\d+, ~deb\d+u\d+, ~\d{2}\.\d{2}(\.\d+)*, ~ubuntu\d[\d.]*, ~esm\d*, ~backport\d*, it still contains a '~', OR contains a pre-release word (?<![A-Za-z])(alpha|beta|rc|pre|preview|prerelease|milestone|candidate)([._-]?\d+)?(?![A-Za-z]), OR a VCS/nightly/dev marker (git|svn|hg|bzr|cvs|darcs)(hex|digits)|nightly|dev|snapshot, OR a +YYYYMMDD date snapshot. Security/stable rebuild suffixes (-1ubuntu0.22.04.1, +deb11u1, +b1, +nmu1, +esm1, +dfsg, +really2.2-1, -0.1, kaliN, +rpiN) and stable backport tildes (~bpo11+1, ~deb12u1, ubuntu0~16.04.4, ubuntu2~22.04.1) are STABLE.

unstableMarkers.syntax: ~ not followed by a stable backport token (bpo, debNuN, YY.MM, ubuntuN, esm); or words alpha|beta|rc|pre|preview as delimited tokens
(git|svn|hg|bzr|cvs|darcs) followed by digits/hex, or .g<7+hex> at end

semverEquivalents.prerelease: ~ (tilde) in upstream_version; sorts before the release

conventions: Revision is everything after the LAST hyphen; absent revision equals revision 0 and sorts below any non-zero revision (1.0 < 1.0-1).
binNMU +bN (2.9-3 -> 2.9-3+b1); source version unchanged, binary version higher.
NMU: native +nmuN, non-native revision -X.Y (1.5-3 -> 1.5-3.1, 1.0-0.1).
Stable security/point updates +debXuN (X = release major); same-upstream uploads to stable may use ~debXuN.
Backports ~bpoX+N sort below the same version without the tilde and above ~bpo(X-1).
+really rollback without epoch bump (2.3+really2.2-1); never use an epoch for rollbacks.
Ubuntu: ubuntuN (delta), buildN (no-change rebuild), maysync1 < ubuntu1 < willsync1, SRU ubuntu0.N and ubuntu0.<YY.MM>.N, backport ~<YY.MM>.N, +esmN (Pro ESM).
Repacked upstream tarballs +dfsg / +ds / +repack are part of upstream_version and stable.
Suites (stable, testing, unstable, *-backports, *-proposed-updates) are archive channels, never in the version string.
knownGaps: +YYYYMMDD date-snapshot detection and bare rc/beta words without tilde are heuristics, not Policy rules.
dpkg treats a non-digit start or odd characters as warnings, not errors; vectors mark them orderable=true.
Mint +mintN and Kali kaliN suffix forms were not verified against distro documents.
Developers Reference text on non-native NMU numbering (-1.1) was truncated in the fetch.

name: Gentoo ebuild version (PMS)
prerelease: _alpha, _beta, _pre, _rc suffixes (+ number); ladder alpha < beta < pre < rc < release < _p.
buildMetadata: None.
postRelease: _p<N> upstream patch release and a trailing letter (1.0a) sort above the bare version.
yankedDeprecated: Not in the version. package.mask and last-rites removal from the tree; GLSA for security; stability is the per-arch KEYWORDS entry (amd64 vs ~amd64).
stableRule: Version must match ^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)*[a-z]?(_(alpha|beta|pre|rc|p)[0-9]*)*(-r[0-9]+)?$ (else unparseable). UNSTABLE iff it has _(alpha|beta|pre|rc)\d*, a date snapshot _p\d{8}, or a live marker component 9999+ ((^|\.)9{4,}(?=$|\.|[a-z_-])). -rN (Gentoo revision) and _p<N> patch releases are STABLE. Real 'stable' is KEYWORDS, not the version string.

unstableMarkers.syntax: live ebuild: 9999 or 9{4,} as a version component

conventions: -rN is a Gentoo-side revision; absent equals -r0 (1.0 == 1.0-r0).
A numeric component with a leading zero compares as a decimal fraction (1.01 < 1.1); more components wins (1.0 < 1.0.0).
A trailing letter is compared after all numeric components (1.0b < 1.0.0).
Suffixes chain (1.0.0_alpha_rc1); if one side has extra suffixes the first extra _p makes it greater, any other makes it smaller.
Snapshots: <last>_pYYYYMMDD (post) or <upcoming>_preYYYYMMDD (pre); live ebuilds use 9999 or 99999999.
_git/_svn/_cvs/_hg suffixes are not Gentoo syntax.
knownGaps: Only the first 100,000 of 220,673 characters of the PMS page were read.
_p\d{8} may misflag a genuine 8-digit patch counter.
Stability via KEYWORDS and package.mask is outside the version string.
No purl type is known for Gentoo.

name: Homebrew formula version (Version/PkgVersion)
prerelease: Tokens alpha[N]|aN, beta[N]|bN, pre[N], rc[N] (case-insensitive, any separator); ladder alpha < beta < pre < rc < release.
buildMetadata: None; all tokens are compared.
epoch: Formula version_scheme (integer, compared before version); not part of the version string.
postRelease: pN and .postN tokens sort above the release; unknown words (-dev, -nightly) also sort above.
yankedDeprecated: Not in the version. Formula DSL deprecate!/disable! or removal from the tap; versioned formulae (name@N) hold older streams.
stableRule: After removing the formula revision suffix _\d+$, UNSTABLE iff the version contains a pre-release token (?<![A-Za-z])(alpha|beta|pre|rc)\d*(?![A-Za-z]) or (?<=\d)[ab]\d+, or equals HEAD / HEAD-<sha>, or has a dev|devel|snapshot|canary|nightly word or VCS word. _N revision, pN and .postN are STABLE.
conventions: _N suffix is the formula revision (rebuild), compared after the version; omitted when 0; carried by OSV and pkg:brew purls.
name@N selects a version stream in the NAME.
HEAD versions are equal to each other and greater than every release.
1 == 1.0 == 1.0.0 (zero tokens equal the absent token).
Bottle rebuild numbers are not part of the version.
knownGaps: Unknown words (-dev, -nightly) sort above the release; do not infer stability from ordering.
a1/b1 tokens may misread a patch letter plus build number.
version_scheme is not in the version string; string-only comparison cannot reproduce Formula-level order.
Casks are not covered.

name: Linux kernel mainline (x.y[.z[.w]][-rcN])
prerelease: -rcN (6.0-rc1 .. rc7) sorts before the release it precedes and after the previous release; stable-queue 6.1.55-rc1 sorts before 6.1.55.
buildMetadata: None for kernel.org versions; distros append their own (-generic, +deb) which belong to the distro scheme.
postRelease: Stable updates add a third component (6.1.55); legacy trees use four (2.6.32.71).
yankedDeprecated: None in the number. Stable/longterm branches are declared end-of-life by the kernel maintainers.
stableRule: Version (optional leading v) must match ^v?\d+\.\d+(\.\d+){0,2}(-rc\d+)?$ or ^next-\d{8}$. UNSTABLE iff it ends in -rc\d+ or is a linux-next tag next-YYYYMMDD. x.y, x.y.z and x.y.z.w are STABLE. Distro kernel strings (6.1.0-18-amd64, 5.14.0-362.el9) are not this scheme.
conventions: Numbering is not semantic: 5.0 followed 4.20; the first component carries no compatibility meaning.
OSV Linux 'versions' arrays use tags with a leading v while ECOSYSTEM range events do not.
OSV GIT ranges carry commit hashes because fixes are backported across stable trees.
Only the name Kernel is supported in OSV.
knownGaps: Ordering is derived, not from a normative comparator.
next- tag naming was not retrieved from a document.
v-prefix mapping between versions arrays and range events is inferred from sample data.

name: Nix/nixpkgs (pname-version, compareVersions)
prerelease: Only the literal component 'pre' (0.12pre12876) sorts below the release and below end of string; rc/beta/alpha are ordinary words and sort ABOVE the release.
buildMetadata: None; '+' stays inside a word component.
postRelease: <last>-unstable-YYYY-MM-DD sorts above <last> and below the next release; extra numeric component sorts above.
yankedDeprecated: Not in the version. meta.knownVulnerabilities / insecure / broken attributes, or removal from nixpkgs (alias throws).
stableRule: UNSTABLE iff the version contains the word unstable (-unstable-YYYY-MM-DD, 0-unstable-..., legacy unstable-...), a delimited pre-release word (alpha|beta|rc|pre|preview|prerelease|milestone|candidate)\d*, a VCS word (git|svn|hg|bzr|cvs followed by digits/hex), or nightly/dev/devel/snapshot/canary. Plain dotted numbers, date versions and -bin style tags are STABLE. Ordering must not be used to detect pre-releases (rc sorts above).
conventions: Derivation name pname-version splits at the first '-' not followed by a letter, so a version must start with a digit.
'.' and '-' are interchangeable component separators; '_' and '+' are not.
nixpkgs: <last-release>-unstable-YYYY-MM-DD for commits, 0-unstable-YYYY-MM-DD when no release exists.
Components that parse as int compare numerically; a word is below a number (2.3a < 2.3.1); end of string is below numbers and words (1.0 < 1.0.0, 1.0 < 1.0a).
Channels (nixos-unstable) are branches and unrelated to -unstable- in versions.
knownGaps: No authoritative definition of 'stable' for Nix versions; markers are nixpkgs conventions plus common upstream words.
Components overflowing int fall back to string comparison (untested).
purl type for Nix is unverified.

name: RPM (epoch:version-release)
prerelease: Tilde: 2.0~rc1 sorts before 2.0 and before end of string; tilde also appears in the release field. Legacy Fedora convention Release: 0.N.rc1 sorts below Release 1.
buildMetadata: None. Separators (. _ +) are interchangeable and ignored; any alphanumeric text is compared.
epoch: Integer before ':' in EVR, default 0, most significant component.
postRelease: Caret: 2.0^20250611 sorts after 2.0 but before 2.0.1 (snapshot after base); or an extra segment (2.0.post1).
yankedDeprecated: No in-band flag. Repositories drop builds; errata supersede with higher release; Obsoletes/Provides tags; epoch bump for backwards moves.
stableRule: A version is STABLE unless its version or release contains: a '~' (prerelease); a '^' (snapshot); a delimited pre-release word (alpha|beta|rc|pre|preview|prerelease|milestone|candidate)\d*; a VCS/nightly/dev marker (git|svn|hg|bzr|cvs|darcs followed by digits/hex, \d{8}g[0-9a-f]{7,}, nightly, dev, snapshot); or a release matching ^0(\.|$) (legacy Fedora pre-release/snapshot Release: 0.N.*). Dist tags and z-stream suffixes (.el9, .el9_3, .el9_3.5, .fc40, .module+el8.9.0+..., .amzn2023, .lp155, .mga9, .ph5, 150500.3.12.1) are STABLE rebuilds; a '~' that precedes only a stable backport token (~bpo, ~deb, ~esm, ~NN.NN) is also stable.

unstableMarkers.syntax: ~ in version or release; delimited alpha|beta|rc|pre words; release ^0\.

conventions: RELEASE is the packaging revision, compared only after VERSION is equal; reset to 1 when VERSION changes.
Dist tags %{?dist}: .el9, .el9_3 (z-stream), .fc40, .module+el8.x, .amzn2023, .lp155, .mga9, .ph5; SUSE release counters like 150500.3.12.1.
Fedora snapshot field after caret: <date>.<rev>, <date><scm><rev>, <number>.<scm><rev>, scm in git|svn|hg|snap or one letter.
Version: 0 when upstream never chose a version.
Underscore as visual separator (1.2~pre1, 1.2_final) has no ordering effect.
Non-ASCII characters are ignored by rpmvercmp (1.1.a-alpha == 1.1.b-beta equal).
Dependency comparison skips RELEASE when the constraint has none.
knownGaps: The ^0\. release rule is a convention and can false-positive on distros using release 0 for other purposes.
rpm releases that introduced ~ and ^ are from memory; RHEL 7 (rpm 4.11) lacks ^.
Dist-tag shapes for Mageia, Photon, Azure Linux, openEuler are observed, not specified.
Missing-epoch semantics in dependency constraints were not verified.

name: Wolfi/Chainguard apk (go-apk strict subset, melange -rN)
prerelease: One optional _alpha|_beta|_pre|_rc suffix (+ number); sorts below the release (none is ranked above rc).
buildMetadata: None; ~hash is rejected by go-apk.
epoch: None. melange 'epoch' is the apk -rN revision, not an RPM/dpkg epoch.
postRelease: One optional _cvs|_svn|_git|_hg|_p suffix (+ number) after the pre suffix; cvs < svn < git < hg < p.
yankedDeprecated: No in-band flag. Rolling repository index; superseded builds are removed; advisories are published as OSV records with fixed X-rN.
stableRule: Version must match the go-apk regex ^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)*[a-z]?((_alpha|_beta|_pre|_rc)[0-9]*)?((_cvs|_svn|_git|_hg|_p)[0-9]*)?(-r[0-9]+)?$ (else unparseable). UNSTABLE iff it has _(alpha|beta|pre|rc)\d* or _(git|hg|cvs|svn)\d*. -rN (melange epoch / security rebuild), _p<N> and a trailing letter are STABLE.
conventions: package.epoch N in melange renders as <name>-<version>-rN.apk; monotonically increasing from 0.
Snapshot pkgver <last>_git<YYYYMMDD>, and 0_git<YYYYMMDD> for projects with no release (seen in 2 of 120 sampled Wolfi packages).
Version streams are separate package names (php-8.1, php-8.2); apk add foo=~4.5.6 is a dependency-expression prefix match, not a version syntax.
go-apk treats 1.0 == 1.0-r0 and 1.01 == 1.1; C apk-tools does not.
knownGaps: OSV does not state which comparator Wolfi/Chainguard consumers use; C apk-tools semantics differ on 1.0 vs 1.0-r0, leading zeros, ~hash and repeated suffixes.
Docker Hardened Images and CleanStart are mapped here by assumption.
Only a 120-package sample of Wolfi definitions was read.

name: conda VersionOrder
prerelease: No formal syntax: any letter component such as `a`, `b`, `rc`, `alpha`, `beta` (`1.0a1`, `1.2.beta3`) sorts below the release because strings sort below ints; `dev` sorts below everything at its position.
buildMetadata: `+local` is compared like extra components only when the main versions are equal; an alphabetic local sorts BELOW the plain version (`1.0+abc < 1.0`), a numeric one above; not a stability signal by itself.
epoch: `N!` prefix, default 0, same idea as PEP 440.
postRelease: String `post` is greater than any other string at its position (`1.1.post1 > 1.1`); stable.
yankedDeprecated: No yank in the version. Channel mechanisms (repodata `removed`, repodata patches, anaconda.org `broken` label) exist but were not verified.
stableRule: Stable iff no component string other than `post` is present, no `dev`, and no `+local`; bare tags (e.g. `1.1.parallel`) are undecidable from the string, so treat as unstable only if a known pre-release word.

unstableMarkers.syntax: component string a|alpha|b|beta|c|rc|pre|preview with optional digits

semverEquivalents.prerelease: Letters inside components, ordered as case-insensitive strings below ints.
semverEquivalents.buildMetadata: `+local`, compared (unlike SemVer); conda's separate build string/number is not part of the version.
semverEquivalents.postRelease: `post` string, above everything at its position.

conventions: `-` is accepted and converted to `_` when the version has no underscore, so `1.0-SNAPSHOT` is a valid tag version.
`1.0rc1 < 1.0.dev1` (dev after a dot is a new component), opposite to PEP 440.
Letter-suffix versions (openssl `1.0.1a`) sort below `1.0.1`; trailing `_` (`1.0.1_`) is the documented workaround and sorts lowest.
A component starting with a letter gets an implicit leading 0 (`1.1.a1 == 1.1.0a1`); `1.1 == 1.1.0`.
knownGaps: Ground truth is py-rattler cross-checked with the VersionOrder docstring ladder, not conda's own Python.
Stability of bare tags is undecidable from the string.
Registry-level removal mechanisms not verified.

name: Coursier / sbt version ordering
prerelease: Tag levels: dev -6 < unknown -5 < alpha -4 < beta -3 < rc/cr -2 < snapshot -1 < ga/final/empty 0 < sp/bin 1; unknown tags are BELOW alpha (pre-release), unlike Maven.
buildMetadata: `+...` is parsed as BuildMetadata and ignored in comparison (SemVer-aware); `1.0+build.5 == 1.0`.
postRelease: `sp` and `bin` tags sort above the release.
yankedDeprecated: None in the version scheme; resolution uses Maven/Ivy repositories, which have no yank.
stableRule: Unstable iff any tag has level < 0 (dev, unknown tag, alpha, beta, rc, snapshot); tags ga/final/sp/bin and `+build` metadata are stable.

unstableMarkers.syntax: tag alpha|a|beta|b|rc|cr, or any unknown tag (level < 0)

semverEquivalents.prerelease: Hyphen tags with fixed levels; unknown tags rank below alpha.

conventions: Used by sbt >= 1.3, Scala CLI, Mill; same family as Maven GenericVersion but with its own tag levels.
Scala binary-version suffix `_2.13` is part of the artifactId, not the version; Scala milestones `2.13.0-M5` are an unknown tag (below alpha) and still precede RC1.
`.x`/`.*`/`.+` are treated as max for ranges; `min`/`max` words are special items.
knownGaps: Coined ordering id `custom:coursier`; run via deprecated coursier.core.Version in coursier-core 2.1.26 (the replacement coursier.version.Version was not run).
Disagrees with Maven on unknown qualifiers (below release here, above in Maven), dev rank and build metadata.
Older sbt (< 1.3) uses Ivy ordering, see the ivy entry.

name: Gradle version ordering
prerelease: No pre-release syntax: split on `. - _ +` and digit/letter transitions; `dev` is lowest, unknown strings (ASCII, case-sensitive) next, then rc < snapshot < final < ga < release < sp; any version with an extra string part is BELOW the bare version.
buildMetadata: None: `+` is a separator, so `1.0+build` has a lower string part and sorts BELOW 1.0.
postRelease: `sp` ranks highest among string parts, but `1.0-sp1 < 1.0` because an extra non-numeric part is lower than no part.
yankedDeprecated: None in the version scheme; Gradle component `status` (integration for -SNAPSHOT, release otherwise, default scheme integration < milestone < release) comes from metadata, not a yank flag.
stableRule: Same qualifier word list as maven: unstable iff -SNAPSHOT (status integration), timestamped snapshot, or a conventional pre-release word (alpha, beta, milestone, m, rc, dev, ea, preview, nightly); final/ga/release/sp are stable.

semverEquivalents.prerelease: Any extra string part; only dev/rc/snapshot/final/ga/release/sp carry fixed ranks.

conventions: Trailing zero is significant: `1.0 < 1.0.0`.
Special words are case-insensitive but unknown strings compare case-sensitively (`1.A < 1.B < 1.a`).
Comparing two different-case spellings of one special word returns 0 immediately: `1.0-RC1 == 1.0-rc9`.
Dynamic versions `1.+`, `latest.integration`, `latest.release`.
knownGaps: Gradle docs say sp/final/ga/release are 'higher than any other string part' but versus a bare version they sort lower (verified by running the real source).
Differs from Maven on `1.0 == 1.0.0`, `-final`, `-sp1`, `+build`, `dev` rank; Maven docs note `[1.0,2.0)` is interpreted differently in Gradle.
Stability classes are convention; Gradle itself only exposes status.

name: Apache Ivy latest-revision
prerelease: No syntax: parts split on `. _ - +` and letter/digit boundaries; only `dev` (-1), `rc` (1) and `final` (2) are special; unknown strings (0) sort lexically, `1.0-dev1 < 1.0-alpha1 < 1.0-rc1 < 1.0`.
buildMetadata: None: `+` is a separator and the following word is an ordinary string part.
postRelease: None; `sp`, `ga`, `snapshot` and `release` are not special, and `1.0-final < 1.0`.
yankedDeprecated: None in the version scheme; Ivy descriptors carry a `status` (integration/milestone/release) used by latest.<status> selectors.
stableRule: No engine-level stable flag; apply the maven word list (snapshot, alpha, beta, rc, milestone, dev) to string parts; descriptor status `release` is the registry-level signal.

unstableMarkers.syntax: -SNAPSHOT string part (not special in Ivy ordering)

semverEquivalents.prerelease: Any extra string part; dev < unknown < rc < final.

conventions: Algorithm is inspired by PHP version_compare; 1.0 < 1.0.0 (extra numeric part is higher).
`1.0-RC1 == 1.0-rc2` short-circuit (same code lineage as Gradle).
Custom special words can be configured per Ivy settings; defaults used here.
knownGaps: Coined ordering id `custom:ivy` because no listed id fits (closest is gradle: same dev/rc/final lineage but Gradle adds snapshot/ga/release/sp).
No purl type known for Ivy modules; they are Maven-layout artifacts.
Ivy descriptor `status` semantics were not verified beyond the Gradle docs.

name: Maven ComparableVersion
prerelease: Qualifiers alpha < beta < milestone < rc (= cr) < snapshot, all below the release; a/b/m are shorthand only when directly followed by a digit; case-insensitive.
buildMetadata: None: `+` is an ordinary character folded into a qualifier string (`1.0+build.5` sorts after 1.0); not a stability signal.
postRelease: `sp` (service pack) and a numeric sublist `1.0-1` sort after the release; `ga`, `final`, `release` equal the bare release.
yankedDeprecated: None on Maven Central (components are not removed or modified; no deprecated/deleted flag). Closest: POM `distributionManagement/relocation`.
stableRule: Unstable iff a token matches (?i)(^|[.\-_])(alpha|beta|milestone|rc|cr|snapshot|a\d|b\d|m\d), or `-YYYYMMDD.HHMMSS-N` timestamped snapshot, or by convention dev/ea/preview/pre/nightly/canary; stable otherwise (ga, final, release, sp, -N, jre, android, incubating).

unstableMarkers.syntax: alpha|beta|milestone|rc|cr, or a|b|m followed by a digit, as a qualifier token
-SNAPSHOT suffix (case-insensitive) or timestamped -\d{8}\.\d{6}-\d+$ (sorts AFTER the release)
conventional unknown qualifier dev/ea/preview/pre (sorts AFTER the release in Maven)

semverEquivalents.prerelease: Fixed-rank qualifiers alpha/beta/milestone/rc/snapshot; SemVer 2.0.0 precedence is explicitly not followed.
semverEquivalents.buildMetadata: None; `+` is part of a qualifier string.

conventions: Trailing zeros and ga/final/release are trimmed so `1 == 1.0 == 1.0.0 == 1.0-ga`.
`.qualifier = -qualifier < -number < .number`; list/sublist nesting is created by `-` and by letter/digit transitions.
Unknown qualifiers sort after `sp`, lexically; so `1.0-dev`, `1.0-ea`, `1.0-nightly` are NEWER than 1.0 although semantically pre-releases.
Timestamped snapshot `1.0-20240101.123456-1` is a numeric sublist and sorts after release 1.0.
Version ranges `[1.0,2.0)` include `2.0-rc1`; LATEST/RELEASE are meta-versions, not versions (`ComparableVersion("RELEASE")` equals 0).
Scala `_2.13` artifact suffix is part of the artifactId, not the version; Guava-style `-jre`/`-android` flavours are stable.
knownGaps: Three comparators exist: maven-artifact ComparableVersion 3.x (primary here), Maven 4 master ComparableVersion (differs on ~0.1% of realistic pairs, e.g. `2.0-1` vs `2-3`, and gives `1-sp-1 > 1-ga-1` contrary to the published spec) and maven-resolver GenericVersion (treats `1.0-1 == 1.0.1`, `1-1 == 1.1`, and orders timestamped snapshots after 1.0.1).
Stability of unknown qualifiers (dev, ea, preview, nightly) is convention, not spec; `incubating` treated as stable.
No registry yank/deprecation flag; Clojars policy not checked.

name: PEP 440 (PyPI, pip)
prerelease: Normalised `aN`, `bN`, `rcN` (spellings alpha, beta, c, pre, preview accepted, separators . - _ optional) and `.devN`; all sort before the final, with `.devN` below `aN` below `bN` below `rcN` below the final.
buildMetadata: `+label` is a local version: it IS compared (sorts after the same public version; numeric segments above alphabetic), PyPI rejects uploads containing it, so treat it as a non-public/unstable signal.
epoch: `N!` prefix, integer, implicit 0; a higher epoch outranks every lower-epoch version (`1!1.0 > 2024.1`).
postRelease: `.postN` (also `-N`, `rev`, `r`); sorts after the final and is stable.
yankedDeprecated: PEP 592 yank is per file: `data-yanked` attribute in the simple HTML API, `files[].yanked` (bool or reason string) in the PEP 691 JSON API, `releases[v][i].yanked`/`yanked_reason` in the Warehouse JSON API. Project-level status (PEP 792) lives in simple API `project-status`.
stableRule: Parse with PEP 440; stable iff pre is None and dev is None and local is None (post and epoch are fine); unparseable strings are skipped; skip yanked files unless exactly pinned.

unstableMarkers.syntax: \.dev\d+ (raw [._-]?dev[._-]?\d*), also on post and pre releases

semverEquivalents.prerelease: Only aN/bN/rcN and .devN; arbitrary SemVer identifiers (`-alpha.beta`, `-x.7.z.92`) are invalid; `-rc.1` normalises to rc1.
semverEquivalents.buildMetadata: Local version `+label`, but it participates in ordering unlike SemVer build metadata.
semverEquivalents.epoch: No SemVer equivalent; epoch `N!` overrides all other components.
semverEquivalents.postRelease: No SemVer equivalent; `.postN` sorts after the final.

conventions: Trailing zeros are insignificant (`1.0 == 1.0.0`); `v` prefix, case and the separators `. - _` normalise away.
`1.0-1` is a post-release (stable, newer than 1.0), not a prerelease.
Alternate spellings (alpha, beta, c, pre, preview, rev, r) normalise to a, b, rc, post.
Dev releases of pre/post releases exist (`1.0a1.dev1`, `1.0.post1.dev1`).
Specifier semantics exclude pre-releases unless asked (`>=1.0` skips `1.1a1`); `>V` excludes post-releases of V.
CalVer (`2024.1.15`) is valid.
knownGaps: Yanked cannot be derived from the string; the consumer must carry the registry flag.
Local versions are classed unstable by policy; `packaging.is_prerelease` is False for them.
Legacy non-conforming strings (`1.0-SNAPSHOT`, `1.0.RELEASE`) are unparseable since packaging 22.0; old PyPI data may contain them.
conda uses a different comparator (see conda entry).

name: RubyGems Gem::Version
prerelease: Any ASCII letter in the version makes it a prerelease (`1.0.0.pre`, `.rc1`, `.beta.2`); letter segments compare below numeric ones, so a prerelease sorts below its release, ordered alphabetically (case-sensitive) among letter words.
buildMetadata: None: `+` is invalid and raises; a `-` is rewritten to `.pre.`, so `1.0.0-rc1` becomes `1.0.0.pre.rc1` (a prerelease).
postRelease: None: `post` is just a letter so `1.0.0.post1` is a PRERELEASE and sorts BELOW 1.0.0.
yankedDeprecated: Yank = DELETE /api/v1/gems/yank; the version vanishes from /api/v1/versions and /info, GET /api/v2/rubygems/<g>/versions/<v> returns 404, and the compact index /versions file gets an append-only `<gem> -<version> <md5>` line (leading `-`). JSON `yanked` boolean exists on /api/v1/gems/<g>.json.
stableRule: Stable iff Gem::Version.new(v).prerelease? is false, i.e. no ASCII letter anywhere in the string and no `-`; strip the platform suffix first; skip versions marked yanked.

unstableMarkers.syntax: [a-zA-Z] anywhere in the version, or `-` (rewritten to .pre.)

semverEquivalents.prerelease: Any letter-bearing segment; `-` becomes `.pre.`; no phase semantics (alphabetical).

conventions: Trailing zeros are ignored, also before the first letter (`1.a == 1.0.a == 1.0.0.a`).

Platform is a separate field (`name-version-platform.gem`; compact index writes VERSION-PLATFORM split at the first dash): x86_64-linux, arm64-darwin, java, x64-mingw-ucrt, x86-mswin32-60, etc.; never part of the Gem::Version.
Feeding `1.3.1-java` to Gem::Version yields prerelease `1.3.1.pre.java`; `1.0.0-x86_64-linux` raises.
Prerelease word order is alphabetical (alpha < beta < dev < post < pre < rc), so `dev` builds outrank `beta`.
Empty/nil version is `0`; blank whitespace is stripped; Rational Versioning (3 integers) is recommended.
knownGaps: Reason tokens (dev, snapshot, nightly, milestone) are assigned from the letter text in vectors; RubyGems only knows prerelease.
Whether rubygems.org permits re-pushing a yanked version number was not verified.
Run on Ruby 4.0.7 / RubyGems 4.0.20 only; the sort_key fast path was not diffed against older releases.

name: Apple OS versions and build numbers (macOS, iOS, bundles)
prerelease: build number ending in a lowercase letter (23D5033f) = developer beta; labels "beta"/"RC" in marketing text
buildMetadata: build number in parentheses
postRelease: Rapid Security Response suffix (a) has no tuple
yankedDeprecated: Apple withdraws/replaces builds; no flag
stableRule: marketing X.Y[.Z] tuples are comparable within one platform; stable if build number has no trailing lowercase letter and no beta/RC label; never compare across platforms
conventions: Build number NNLnnnn: train digits, capital letter = minor train, sequence
Old majors get security updates that are newer by date than the latest major
knownGaps: No first-party doc for the build-number structure was retrievable; relies on community explanations (explicitly informal).
Cross-platform marketing numbering (iOS vs macOS vs watchOS) is not unified; do not compare across platforms.

name: Where "highest number wins" or "newest date wins" gives the WRONG latest (LTS lines, back-port point releases, floating majors, 0.x carets)
prerelease: defer to the underlying scheme
buildMetadata: defer
yankedDeprecated: defer
stableRule: meta-rule: true latest = max stable tuple per the underlying scheme; never newest-by-date; old-line point release = line key lower than the max line key; flags/dist-tags/channels decide stability where the string is plain

unstableMarkers.syntax: caret/tilde on 0.x pins the minor: ^0.15.10 resolves to 0.15.22

conventions: META scheme, not a real version format: ordering "none" means defer to the scheme of the package
Real inversions: Django 190/382, Node 465/875; ruff 1/429 (no 0.15.x vs 0.17.x inversion)
knownGaps: Only PyPI datasets have per-file upload time; GitHub published_at can be bulk-edited (actions/checkout released six majors at once).
Docker Hub last_updated is mutable.

name: Browser extension manifest versions (Chrome, Edge, Firefox)
prerelease: none in `version`; use `version_name` or a separate listing/channel; legacy Firefox toolkit format allows pre/a/b/rc
buildMetadata: 4th integer by convention
yankedDeprecated: store delist/block (Chrome Web Store, AMO), browser blocklist by id+version range; no yank flag
stableRule: no string rule: a version is stable unless the store channel/listing or version_name says otherwise; validity: 1-4 integers, each 0-65535 (Chrome), no leading zeros, not all zero
conventions: Fields capped at 65535 on Chrome so YYYYMMDD cannot be one field
Update manifest picks the highest numeric version
Each store keeps its own counter
knownGaps: No pre-release representation, so stability must come from the store channel or version_name.
Overflow of 65535 for CalVer/date fields on Chrome.
AMO's nine-digit allowance is from MDN prose only.

name: CalVer and date-based versions (calver.org)
prerelease: PEP 440 aN/bN/rcN/.devN or -rcN modifier on a CalVer base; yt-dlp style YYYY.M.D.HHMMSS.dev0
buildMetadata: rare +hash
epoch: PEP 440 N! after a scheme switch
postRelease: .postN or same-day counter (.1)
yankedDeprecated: registry-specific (PyPI yank etc.)
stableRule: numeric tuple with no pre/dev part; CalVer shape itself is not unstable; parse integers (2024.02.02 -> 2024.2.2), never compare strings; detect CalVer with calver-detection.json
conventions: Calendar segments YYYY, YY, 0Y, M, 0M, W, 0W, D, 0D plus MAJOR/MINOR/MICRO counters.
Zero-padded months (22.04) are invalid SemVer.
tzdata style YYYYa..z letter suffix.
Major is a year, not a breaking-change signal; SemVer ranges (^) are meaningless
Letter-year tzdata 2024b; ISO date versions (2026-10-01); YYYYMMDD single field
Zero padding (0M/0D) normalised away by PEP 440, illegal in SemVer
knownGaps: No reference implementation; ordering derived from common practice.
Shape alone cannot tell black 24.2.0 or pip 24.0 from a SemVer major; see index.md detector.
Rule B depends on release dates; for registries without dates (Maven Central indexes do, some do not) the YY form is unresolvable.
Calendar semantics (week numbers 0W, YYYY.WW) were not sampled with real packages.
80%/20-version/3-year thresholds were tuned on 22 PyPI/npm/CPython/Node datasets, not a large corpus.

name: Chocolatey packages (NuGet versions)
prerelease: dash suffix (-beta, -rc1, -pre20240101); hidden unless `choco --pre`
buildMetadata: `+` metadata accepted by recent NuGet, ignored
postRelease: 4th numeric segment = package fix (or date)
yankedDeprecated: unlist; community-repo moderation rejection/deprecation (deprecation flag unverified)
stableRule: no dash pre-release label; up to 4 numeric segments (4th = package fix); ordering NuGet-style, labelled sorts below unlabelled
conventions: 4th segment for package fixes must be used consistently
Sibling packages <id>.install, <id>.portable, <id>-nightly
knownGaps: NuGet version reference page not fetched; label comparison rules for legacy NuGet were summarized from general knowledge.
No explicit channels beyond pre-release flag and sibling package IDs.

name: Database majors: PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB
prerelease: PostgreSQL attached alpha/beta/rc/devel (17beta1); MySQL -rc/-dmr
buildMetadata: distro suffix (-0ubuntu0.22.04.1, -MariaDB)
yankedDeprecated: rare out-of-cycle re-release; no flag
stableRule: no attached alpha|beta|rc|devel|dmr token; LTS vs Innovation (MySQL 8.4 vs 9.x) and MariaDB LTS series are NOT in the string, so highest-wins can pick a short-support track
conventions: PostgreSQL: major = first number from 10, first two numbers before (9.6)
MySQL LTS/Innovation tracks
Five-year PG support window
knownGaps: LTS membership for MariaDB is policy text only; not machine-derivable from version.
No upstream machine-readable stability flag for MySQL series (use endoflife.date).

name: Docker / OCI image tags
prerelease: attached aN/bN/rcN or -rc/-beta/-alpha/-pre/-dev/-nightly/-canary/-edge/-snapshot token in the tag; no ordering rule
buildMetadata: `+` is not in the tag alphabet; use `_`/`-` or the org.opencontainers.image.version annotation
yankedDeprecated: no yank in OCI; registries delete tags/manifests; Docker Hub `tag_status` active|inactive; vulnerable images are usually rebuilt under the same tag, so pin by digest
stableRule: stable only if the tag is a fully specified numeric core (>= the image's most specific segment count, e.g. X.Y.Z) with no pre-release token; compare cores only within an identical flavour suffix (text after first `-`); floating aliases (latest, stable, mainline, lts, X, X.Y, codenames), branch/sha/pr tags and digests are NOT pinned versions

semverEquivalents.prerelease: attached letters or hyphen token; unordered

conventions: Flavour suffixes (-alpine3.19, -slim, -bookworm, -perl) partition tags into independent version lines
Cascading aliases: 1.31.8, 1.31, 1, mainline, latest share one digest
Docker Hub last_updated is the last push (rebuilds), not the release date: nginx 1.28.0 shows 2025-12-09, later than 1.29.0 (2025-08-13)
Date tags (20240101, 20240101.1) are CalVer-shaped and carry no stability information
nginx even minor = stable line, odd minor = mainline; both vendor-supported
knownGaps: No normative version grammar; every image author is free to invent one. Flavour/core split is a heuristic and fails for tags like 2024.1-r2 or alpine-3.19-1.2.3 (version after the flavour).
last_updated on Docker Hub is the last push, so rebuilds make an old version look newest; the OCI created annotation is optional.

Anonymous Docker Hub paging stops at 1000 results: observed count: 1381 for nginx, page 11+ returned "pagination offset too large for anonymous requests; sign in to page further". A complete list needs authentication or
GHCR/Quay/ECR use the same OCI grammar; ECR additionally supports tag immutability as a repository setting (can't be assumed).
Whether mainline/odd-minor products are "stable" is vendor policy (nginx treats mainline as production-ready).

name: Git refs (branches, commit SHAs, git-describe strings)
prerelease: none; tag names with -rc1 by convention
buildMetadata: git describe suffix -N-gSHA means N commits after the tag (development snapshot)
yankedDeprecated: none; force-push, branch/tag deletion
stableRule: only refs/tags/<SemVer-like tag> without pre-release part; branches, HEAD, PR refs, commit SHAs and git-describe strings are never stable releases (resolve branch vs tag first: a branch may be named like a version)
conventions: Moving refs used as dependency specifiers (go get @main, uses: o/r@main)
Order only by commit ancestry or commit date; commit dates can be skewed by rebases/cherry-picks
knownGaps: Branch vs tag ambiguity needs the remote ref listing; a bare string cannot be classified reliably.
Commit dates can be authored out of order (rebases, cherry-picks, clock skew), so recency-by-date is itself noisy.
Abbreviated SHAs are ambiguous in large repos.

name: GitHub tags, Releases and GitHub Actions refs
prerelease: Release `prerelease: true` flag (authoritative) and/or SemVer pre-release suffix in the tag
buildMetadata: `+build` accepted in tag names, ignored
yankedDeprecated: no yank; maintainers delete Release/tag, flip `prerelease`, or force-move tags; draft releases are unpublished (exclude)
stableRule: Release `prerelease == false` AND `draft == false` AND tag (prefix-stripped) is SemVer without a pre-release part; order by SemVer of the stripped tag, never by published_at; floating major tags (v4, v1.2) and branch/nightly/latest tags are not pinned versions

unstableMarkers.syntax: ^v?\d+(?:\.\d+)?$ when full vX.Y.Z tags also exist, or ^latest$

conventions: Floating major tags (v1, v4) force-moved to the newest release of the line; back-port releases (v4.4.0 after v7.0.0) are normal
GitHub /releases/latest sorts by created_at (commit date), not version; actions/checkout published v2.8.0 last on 2026-07-20 while latest is v7.0.1
Monorepo prefixes (cli-v2.1.0, @scope/pkg@1.2.3); date-named releases (release-2024-01)
Pin actions by 40-hex commit SHA: immutable, unordered
knownGaps: A repository may tag unrelated things (docs-v2, go/v1) so prefix stripping must be per-repo; false positives are possible.
created_at (commit date) is stable but can be earlier than the previous release when a back-port branch is cut from old commits; sorting by it can still mis-order close releases.
Tag API lists tags by ref name, not date; fetch Releases for dates.
Draft/prerelease flags only exist for Releases, not bare tags. A bare tag v2.0.0-rc.1 is detected by name only.

name: Go toolchain versions (go1.27.3, go1.27rc3) and module pseudo-versions
prerelease: goX.YrcN / goX.YbetaN attached; go.dev/dl `stable: false`
buildMetadata: module +incompatible
yankedDeprecated: modules: go.mod `retract`; toolchain: none
stableRule: go.dev/dl JSON `stable == true` (excludes rc/beta); order 1.21 < 1.21rc1 < 1.21rc2 < 1.21.0 < 1.21.1 (bare language version lowest); module pseudo-versions are snapshots
conventions: Language version (1.21) != toolchain (go1.21.0)
Two newest major lines supported; both released simultaneously
Pseudo-versions for untagged commits
knownGaps: dl JSON has no dates; dates come from the module proxy .info Time for golang.org/toolchain (sampled for 6 versions).
Pre-1.21 numbering (go1.20 first release) needs special-casing.

name: Java / OpenJDK version strings (JEP 223), EA builds, legacy 1.8.0_xxx
prerelease: -ea (any -PRE per JEP 223) sorts below the same VNUM
buildMetadata: +BUILD counts in comparison (unlike SemVer); -OPT may not
yankedDeprecated: superseded by quarterly update; no flag
stableRule: no -PRE (-ea) and no -SNAPSHOT/-internal; compare VNUM element-wise, then PRE (below none), then BUILD numerically; LTS is vendor policy (-LTS in OPT is informational)
conventions: Quarterly update releases for every supported line
LTS every two years (vendor-defined)
knownGaps: JEP 322 text and Adoptium API not fetched; cadence is stated from knowledge.
The JEP page uses $SECURITY, not $PATCH; $PATCH fourth element is described as free for downstream.

name: JetBrains Marketplace plugins and IDE build numbers
prerelease: upload channel other than Stable (eap, beta, alpha, nightly) and/or SemVer pre-release suffix
buildMetadata: SemVer + (rare)
yankedDeprecated: Marketplace `isHidden` / delist; no consumer-visible yank flag
stableRule: plugin update uploaded to the default (empty) Stable channel with no SemVer pre-release part; IDE build numbers (243.12818.47) compare as numeric tuples; EAP/SNAPSHOT builds excluded
conventions: since-build/until-build compatibility ranges with .* wildcard
IDE marketing versions are CalVer (2024.1.2) alongside build numbers
Channels are opt-in custom repositories
knownGaps: Public listing of channel per version needs the Marketplace API (not fetched here).
Nightly channel naming is user-defined (docs list eap/alpha/beta only).

name: Letter-suffix and encoded schemes: zlib, libpng, curl, bash, sqlite
prerelease: libpng attached beta/rc (1.6.44beta01); bash -alpha/-beta/-rc; curl rc- tag prefix; zlib .f dev snapshot
buildMetadata: bash (1) build counter; zlib -motley
postRelease: openssl-style letters (not in this group); bash patchlevel is part of the tuple
yankedDeprecated: none
stableRule: parse numeric tuple; stable if no pre-release word; sqlite integer X*1000000+Y*1000+Z maps 1:1 to X.Y.Z
conventions: Integer encoding of dotted versions (sqlite 3045000)
Underscore tags (curl-8_23_0)
Patchlevel counters outside the release number (bash)

Distro-patched versions (e.g. bash 5.1-6ubuntu1) are separate.

name: Linux kernel (mainline, stable, longterm, -rc, linux-next)
prerelease: -rcN sorts before X.Y; next-YYYYMMDD is linux-next snapshot
buildMetadata: distro/ABI suffix (-45-generic), -rtN
yankedDeprecated: superseded by next .Z; releases.json `iseol`
stableRule: no -rc/next-/-dirty suffix; mainline X.Y, stable X.Y.Z, longterm X.Y.Z; tree (mainline|stable|longterm) is not in the string (releases.json moniker); pre-2.6 odd minors are development

Distro kernels (5.14.0-427.el9) are a different axis from upstream

Distro versions need distro-specific comparison (RPM/dpkg).

name: Node.js runtime (even/odd lines, LTS codenames, nightly/rc/v8-canary/test dists)
prerelease: -rc.N; separate dist directories: nightly (-nightlyYYYYMMDD<sha>), v8-canary, test
buildMetadata: none
yankedDeprecated: superseded; `security: true` marks security releases
stableRule: from nodejs.org/dist/index.json only (the release dist); max SemVer for latest; recommended = max among entries with `lts != false`; rc/nightly/v8-canary/test come from other dist dirs
conventions: LTS is a per-line codename (lts field) not in the string
Even/odd rule until Node 26; from 27 annual October branch, Alpha phase, every line LTS
LTS point releases routinely newer by date than newest Current (465/875 inversions)
knownGaps: LTS promotion occurs in October; a snapshot taken before that shows the new line as Current.
lts can only be read from index.json (or endoflife.date), not from the string.

name: npm dist-tags as a channel signal (SemVer versions with unstable channels)
prerelease: SemVer pre-release part plus dist-tag membership (canary, next, experimental, nightly, beta, rc, alpha, insiders, dev)
buildMetadata: ignored (SemVer)
yankedDeprecated: `npm deprecate` sets `deprecated` on the packument version; `npm unpublish` within limits; no yank
stableRule: no SemVer pre-release part AND not only reachable via a non-latest unstable dist-tag; "recommended latest" = the `latest` dist-tag; never pick by publish time; 0.0.0-experimental-<sha>-<date> sorts lowest yet is newest
conventions: Per-line dist-tags (backport, next-14, v3-latest): `backport` = last published back-port, not the best old-line version
Date/sha prerelease identifiers: 19.3.0-canary-<sha8>-<yyyymmdd>
knownGaps: Dist-tags are mutable; a snapshot is needed to classify.
The packument time map has a modified/created pair and per-version times; unpublished versions drop out.
A publisher may tag latest on an old line (rare).

name: OpenSSL (letter-suffix patch releases <= 1.1.1; SemVer-style from 3.0)
prerelease: -alphaN/-betaN (3.0+ and pre-1.1.0 -betaN/-preN); GitHub `prerelease: true`
buildMetadata: distro suffix (1.1.1k-fips)
postRelease: trailing letters for <= 1.1.1 (1.1.1w > 1.1.1), compare (length, lexical): z < za
yankedDeprecated: none; fixed in next patch; EOL on policy page
stableRule: no -alpha/-beta/-dev; for <= 1.1.1 trailing letters are post-release (stable); true latest = max tuple, not newest by date (multiple lines release same day)
conventions: LTS lines (1.1.1, 3.0, 3.5) shipped concurrently with non-LTS lines

prerelease: none; any non-numeric tail in a dot-part sorts BELOW the bare number (1.2.3-beta < 1.2.3)
buildMetadata: none; `+x` tail also sorts below the bare number (differs from SemVer)
yankedDeprecated: manifest PR removed/reverted in winget-pkgs; no yank flag

name: Bioconductor (R x.y.z with parity)

buildMetadata: No build metadata.
yankedDeprecated: Packages are deprecated in release N and removed in N+1 (removed-packages page); no per-version flag.

Release numbering of Bioconductor itself not covered by the rules page.

name: Cargo / crates.io (Rust semver crate)
prerelease: SemVer -<ident>(.<ident>)*; lower than the release; requirements exclude pre-releases unless the requirement itself names one on the same X.Y.Z.
buildMetadata: +meta accepted; the semver crate Ord DOES compare it as a final tiebreak (1.0.0 < 1.0.0+9 < 1.0.0+a); Cargo ignores it for matching; the index forbids two versions differing only by build. Not a stability signal.
yankedDeprecated: Registry index field yanked:true per version (cargo yank / --undo); yanked versions are skipped for new resolution but lockfiles and downloads still work. No per-version deprecation flag.
stableRule: Stable iff no pre-release part and not yanked. 0.y.z is stable.

semverEquivalents.buildMetadata: same syntax; compared by the crate, ignored by Cargo matching; -sys crates use it for bundled C library version

conventions: 0.y.z compatibility boundary is the left-most non-zero component.
Caret is the default operator; bare * is rejected by crates.io.
rust_version (MSRV) field in the index.
knownGaps: crates.io publish-time rejection text for build metadata was not located.
Build-metadata ordering in the crate differs from semver.org.

name: Clojars / Leiningen / tools.deps (Maven order)
prerelease: Qualifier after -: alpha < beta < milestone < rc=cr < snapshot < release(=final=ga) < sp; unknown qualifiers (dev, nightly, foo) sort ABOVE the release.

postRelease: -sp<N> and numeric sub-lists (1.0-1) are post-releases.
yankedDeprecated: None: Clojars releases are immutable and deletion is discouraged and by caretaker request. No flag.
stableRule: Stable iff no qualifier among alpha/beta/milestone/rc/cr/snapshot/dev/nightly/pre/preview and no timestamped snapshot form. Unknown qualifiers cannot be detected by ordering and need name matching.
conventions: Tokenizer splits on . - _ and digit/letter transitions; trailing 0/final/ga/release trimmed.
Hyphen starts a sub-list, dot continues the list.
SNAPSHOT deploys are mutable; releases immutable.
knownGaps: Maven ComparableVersion and Maven Resolver GenericVersion disagree (1.0-1 vs 1.0.1); vectors use the Resolver.
Clojars SNAPSHOT page not fetched.

name: CocoaPods (Pod::Version)
prerelease: RubyGems segments: a letter segment (1.0.0.beta2, 1.0.0a) or semver-style -id (1.0.0-rc.1) sorts below the release; prerelease? is true for any letter or hyphen.
buildMetadata: +meta accepted and stripped before segment compare, but <=> falls back to a full-string tiebreak; not a stability signal.
postRelease: An extra numeric segment (1.0.0.1) is above 1.0.0.
yankedDeprecated: Podspec spec.deprecated = true and spec.deprecated_in_favor_of (package-level). Trunk specs cannot be deleted.
stableRule: Stable iff, after removing +meta, the string has no letter and no hyphen. Note 1.1.1a and 1.0.0-1 count as pre-release.
conventions: Any number of segments; ~> 1.0 means >=1.0 <2.0.
Podfile can depend on :git/:tag/:branch/:commit instead of versions.
knownGaps: 1.0.0-1 is prerelease? but sorts above 1.0.0.
== ignores +meta while <=> breaks ties by string; rubygems id is approximate for Pod::Version hyphen forms.

name: Composer / Packagist
prerelease: Words after the numeric core: -dev < -alpha[N] (a) < -beta[N] (b) < -RC[N] < release; spellings normalized (rc.1 -> RC1).
buildMetadata: +build is stripped by normalize; not a stability signal.
postRelease: -patch[N] / -p[N] / -pl[N] sorts ABOVE the release and is stable.
yankedDeprecated: Package-level abandoned (true or replacement name) in composer.json/Packagist. No per-version yank flag found.
stableRule: Stable iff parseStability(normalized) is 'stable' (no dev/alpha/beta/RC word, not a dev-* or N.x-dev branch). patch/p/pl suffixes are stable. Always normalize before comparing.
conventions: Branch versions dev-<name> and numeric branches N.x-dev; extra.branch-alias maps a branch to a version.
minimum-stability (default stable) and prefer-stable filter by stability; per-requirement @dev flags.
Up to 4 numeric parts; v prefix removed.
knownGaps: Comparator in composer/semver does not normalize (1.0.0 < 1.0.0.0).
parseStability('master') says stable; treat bare master as a branch.

name: Conan 2 (ConanCenter)
prerelease: Text after the first - (before +): lower than the same core; ranges exclude pre-releases unless include_prerelease or resolve_prereleases=True.
buildMetadata: +build after the last +; compared among non-pre-releases; not a stability signal.
yankedDeprecated: Recipe attribute deprecated (warning); packages removed with conan remove. No yank flag.
stableRule: Stable iff the part after the first - (before +) is empty. Letter patches like 1.1.1w and PEP 440 forms like 1.0.0.dev1 are NOT pre-releases to Conan.
conventions: Any number of segments and lowercase letters; trailing zeros ignored.
Recipe and package revisions (RREV/PREV) order builds of one version.
ConanCenter uses cci.YYYYMMDD for unreleased upstreams.
knownGaps: Mixed digit/letter patches give a non-transitive order (1.1.1a vs 1.1.9 vs 1.1.10).
Version() accepts any string; 'no digits' is treated as unparseable downstream.

name: CPAN (decimal and dotted version.pm)

buildMetadata: No build metadata.
yankedDeprecated: No per-version flag found; deletion moves a release to BackPAN. MetaCPAN deprecation key not verified.
stableRule: Stable iff the version has no underscore (is_alpha false) and the distribution is not -TRIAL / release_status stable.

unstableMarkers.syntax: underscore inside the version, or -TRIAL[N] in the distribution name

conventions: Decimal 1.02 is v1.20.0 (groups of three digits), dotted needs a v or two dots; so 1.10 < 1.2 < 1.9.
Moving from decimal to dotted can go backwards (1.23 = v1.230.0).
knownGaps: Older docs say alpha sorts below the plain version; installed 0.9934 does not.
Deprecation mechanics unverified.

buildMetadata: No build metadata.
yankedDeprecated: Packages are archived wholesale (moved to Archive/, all versions still downloadable); no per-version flag.
stableRule: Stable iff the version parses and the 4th component is below 9000 (convention).
conventions: '.' and '-' are equivalent separators (1.2-3 == 1.2.3); trailing zeros ignored.
At least two components for package_version; components are integers (0.9 < 0.75).
knownGaps: R not installed; ordering from a port of util.c.
CRAN does not enforce the .9000 convention.

name: Go modules (MVS, pseudo-versions)
prerelease: vX.Y.Z-<pre>; lower than the release. Pseudo-versions (vX.0.0-yyyymmddhhmmss-sha, vX.Y.Z-pre.0.ts-sha, vX.Y.(Z+1)-0.ts-sha) are pre-releases that sort above their base and below the next tag.
buildMetadata: +meta ignored in compare; +incompatible marks a v2+ tag without go.mod and is a normal release; not a stability signal.
epoch: Major version path suffix /vN plays the epoch role.
yankedDeprecated: go.mod retract directive (read from the module's latest version) hides versions from list/latest; '// Deprecated:' comment before module deprecates the whole module. Not in the version string.
stableRule: Stable iff valid vX.Y.Z[+meta] with no pre-release part (pseudo-versions are pre-releases) and not retracted. v0.x is stable here even though go.dev calls it 'unstable' compatibility-wise. @latest prefers highest release, then pre-release, then pseudo-version.

semverEquivalents.prerelease: identical; pseudo-version is a pre-release encoding a commit

conventions: Mandatory lowercase v prefix; x/mod/semver also accepts v1 and v1.2 shorthands.
Module path must end /vN for N>=2.
Minimal version selection: highest of required minimums, never newest.
knownGaps: IsPseudoVersion regex reconstructed from behaviour plus docs.
v1.2.3-20191109021931-sha is NOT a pseudo-version despite the lookalike.

name: Hackage (PVP / Cabal Version)
prerelease: None; version tags are unsupported. Pre-release-like states are package candidates, not version strings.
buildMetadata: No build metadata.
postRelease: None; extra components are patch-like.
yankedDeprecated: Registry: preferred-versions (normal / unpreferred / deprecated) and package-level deprecated flag via /package/:p/preferred and /deprecated.
stableRule: Every parseable N(.N)* version is a normal release; exclude versions the registry lists as deprecated or unpreferred.
conventions: Component list ordering: 1 < 1.0 < 1.0.0 (no zero padding).
Major version is the first TWO components A.B.
^>= operator and mandatory upper bounds.
knownGaps: Leading zeros in components unverified.
Exact JSON shape of deprecated/unpreferred lists not fetched.

name: Helm charts (Chart.yaml version)
prerelease: SemVer -<pre>; lower than the release; hidden unless --devel (equivalent to >0.0.0-0) or the constraint names a pre-release.
buildMetadata: +meta allowed (1.2.3-alpha.1+ef365), ignored in compare; replaced by _ in OCI tags; not a stability signal.
yankedDeprecated: Chart.yaml deprecated: true (and the same flag in the repo index.yaml entry). No yank.

Two version axes: chart version and appVersion.
OCI tags replace + with _.
knownGaps: Docs say not enforced strictly and not updated for Helm 4.

name: Hex (Elixir Version)
prerelease: Strict SemVer -<pre>; lower than the release; integer ids < string ids.
buildMetadata: +build accepted and ignored in compare (compare returns :eq); not a stability signal.
yankedDeprecated: mix hex.retire PACKAGE VERSION REASON (renamed, deprecated, security, invalid, other) sets retirement metadata on the release; still resolvable. mix hex.publish --revert within one hour removes.

conventions: ~> pessimistic operator (~> 2.0 = >=2.0.0 and <3.0.0).
All three numeric parts are required.
Retirement reasons are informational; resolution is not blocked.
knownGaps: Whether hex.pm accepts build metadata at publish time was not verified.

name: Julia VersionNumber / Pkg registry
prerelease: -<ident>(.<ident>)* (hyphen optional if the first id starts with a letter); lower than the release; a bare trailing - is the lowest pre-release.
buildMetadata: +build exists and IS compared (1.0.0 < 1.0.0+1 < 1.0.0+a); trailing + is a supremum sentinel; not a stability signal.
yankedDeprecated: Registry Versions.toml yanked = true per version. No deprecation flag found.

conventions: Everything except the major is optional; v prefix optional and case-insensitive.
Compat: caret default, ^0.2.3 = [0.2.3,0.3.0).
Pkg compat bounds use major.minor.patch only.
knownGaps: Ported from Julia source, not executed.
Registrator policy on pre-release publication not located.

name: LuaRocks rockspec versions
prerelease: Words alpha/beta/pre/rc get negative weights so they sort below the release; dev/scm/cvs get huge positive weights and sort above every release.
buildMetadata: No build metadata; a + breaks the tokenizer.
postRelease: Rockspec revision -N (packaging) compared last.
yankedDeprecated: None found in the rockspec; luarocks.org management not examined.
stableRule: Stable iff no alpha/beta/pre/rc word and not dev/scm/cvs. Revisions (-2) do not make it unstable.
conventions: version-revision form; revision bumps for rockspec fixes.
scm/dev rocks build from source control.
== compares component count so 1.0 ~= 1.0.0 while < treats them equal.
knownGaps: Leading v is not stripped (v1.0 sorts as 0.118.0).
Rockspec format doc not fetched.
Order is not consistent across lengths.

name: NuGet (SemVer 2 + 4-part legacy)
prerelease: Hyphen label after Major[.Minor[.Patch[.Revision]]]; any label is lower than the release; labels compared case-insensitively, numeric < alphanumeric.
buildMetadata: +meta accepted (SemVer2), ignored in compare, normalized away; not a stability signal.
postRelease: 4th Revision numeric segment acts like a legacy post-release component (1.0.0.1 > 1.0.0).
yankedDeprecated: nuget.org: unlist (listed=false; hidden from search, still restorable by exact version) and separate deprecation metadata (Legacy, Critical Bugs, Other + alternate package). Neither is in the version string.
stableRule: Stable iff there is no hyphen label. Revision (4th part) and metadata do not make it unstable. Resolution picks stable only unless the range names a pre-release.
conventions: Missing parts are zero: 1, 1.0, 1.0.0 and 1.0.0.0 are equal; leading zeros normalized (01.0.0 -> 1.0.0).
Floating versions 1.* and 1.0.0-* ; lowest applicable version wins on restore.
Interval ranges [1.0,2.0).
knownGaps: Docs sentence about 'reverse alphabetical order' mis-describes the displayed descending list.
SemVer1 label rules only matter for old clients.

name: opam (Debian-style)
prerelease: Convention only: ~suffix (1.0~beta) sorts before 1.0; opam has no pre-release syntax and -rc1 sorts ABOVE the release.
buildMetadata: No build metadata; + suffix sorts after the base (variants such as 4.14.0+flambda) and is normally stable.
postRelease: +suffix or -N revision (last - splits a Debian-style revision).
yankedDeprecated: opam file flags: avoid-version (lowest solver priority) and deprecated (same plus message). Flags live in the package's opam file.
stableRule: Stable iff there is no ~ in the version, it is not dev/master and has no +dev/+gitYYYY marker, and flags lack avoid-version/deprecated. Beware -rc and -beta forms sort above the release.
conventions: Alternating non-digit/digit run comparison; ~ < end < letters < other symbols.
Package identity is name.version; version is everything after the first dot of the directory name.
knownGaps: Ported from OCaml source, not executed.
Pre-release classification is convention, not specified.

name: pub (Dart / Flutter)
prerelease: SemVer -<pre>; lower than the release; pub prefers stable and ^X.Y.Z upper bound is <(X+1).0.0-0 so next-major pre-releases are excluded.
buildMetadata: +build accepted and ORDERED after the plain release (1.0.0 < 1.0.0+1); Dart uses +N as a non-API-changing bump. Not a stability signal.
postRelease: +N build suffix behaves like a post-release (pub ordering).
yankedDeprecated: Per version retracted:true (pub.dev Admin, within 7 days; restorable). Package-level isDiscontinued (+replacedBy). Both are API/registry fields.
stableRule: Stable iff no pre-release part and not retracted.
conventions: 0.x shifted one slot: 0.1.2 -> 0.2.0 is breaking; ^0.1.2 = >=0.1.2 <0.2.0.
SDK constraints use the same grammar.
knownGaps: pub_semver accepts leading zeros (01.0.0, 1.0.0-01); pub.dev publish validation not tested.
How pub.dev computes 'latest' is documented only informally.

name: rebar3 (vendored ec_semver, Hex packages)
prerelease: -<id>(.<id>)*; lower than the release; the FIRST id is compared as text even when numeric (-10 < -2), later numeric ids as integers.
buildMetadata: +build accepted and compared as a final tiebreak; not a stability signal.
postRelease: 4th numeric part (minpatch).
yankedDeprecated: Hex retirement (see hex); rebar3 sources read do not interpret it. Git deps use tag/branch/ref pins in rebar.lock.
stableRule: Stable iff the parse succeeds and the pre-release list is empty. A bare Hex dependency ignores pre-releases; is_prerelease_or_build checks for - or + in the constraint.
conventions: Optional v prefix, 1 to 4 numeric parts, missing parts are zero.
Non-Hex deps: versions informational only.
knownGaps: Executed parser accepted 1.0.0-x-y though the .peg looks stricter.
May use verl for some Hex paths; not confirmed.

name: SemVer 2.0.0 / npm node-semver
prerelease: Suffix -<ident>(.<ident>)*; any pre-release is lower than the same X.Y.Z release; numeric ids < alphanumeric ids, ASCII order, more ids is higher.
buildMetadata: +<ident>(.<ident>)* exists, is ignored for precedence, is not a stability signal.
yankedDeprecated: npm: version.deprecated message in the packument (npm deprecate, ranges allowed); unpublish removes. dist-tags are aliases, not versions. SemVer itself defines nothing.
stableRule: Stable iff the parsed version has no pre-release part (no hyphen before the first +). Build metadata and 0.y.z do not make it unstable. Strings that do not parse (latest, next, dist-tags) are not versions.
conventions: npm strips a leading v or = and trims whitespace; loose mode accepts leading zeros.
Pre-releases only satisfy a range when a comparator has the same [major,minor,patch] and a pre-release, unless includePrerelease.
dist-tags (latest, next) are registry aliases rejected if they parse as a semver range.
knownGaps: Stable filter is a consumer convention; semver.org does not define 'stable'.
sort() tie order for build-only differences is implementation behaviour.

name: SwiftPM (git tags / registry)
prerelease: SemVer -<ident>(.<ident>)* (empty ids tolerated); lower than the release; numeric ids via Int() < alphanumeric. Range bounds without a pre-release exclude pre-releases.
buildMetadata: +meta accepted, ignored in compare and hash; not a stability signal.
yankedDeprecated: No flag for git tags. Registry (SE-0292) may list a release with a 410 Gone problem document ('removed from the registry'). No deprecation flag found.
stableRule: Stable iff the tag parses (strip one leading lowercase v, allow 2-part) and has no pre-release identifiers. Branch/revision refs are not versions.

semverEquivalents.prerelease: identical (one hyphenated id is common: prerelease-2024-01-15)

conventions: Tags without and with v and 2-part tags collapse to one version; most specific tag kept.
Version-specific tags (@swift-5.9 suffix) override plain tags when present.
from: means up-to-next-major.
knownGaps: Ported from Swift source, not executed in Swift.
Int() accepts leading zeros and a + sign.

name: Terraform Registry (go-version)
prerelease: SemVer-like -<pre> (hyphen optional in go-version); lower than the release; constraints other than = never match pre-releases.
buildMetadata: +meta accepted, ignored; not a stability signal.
yankedDeprecated: Module owner can remove one or all versions via the registry UI. No yank or deprecation flag in the docs read.
stableRule: Stable iff go-version Prerelease() is empty. Pre-releases are selectable only with an exact = constraint.
conventions: Release tags must be semver optionally prefixed v; other tags ignored.
~> allows only the right-most component to increment.
Any number of numeric segments and an optional v prefix.
knownGaps: go-version orders 1.0.0-alpha.beta below 1.0.0-alpha (not total for such inputs).
Provider deprecation flags not found.
Behaviour is go-version v1.9.0.

name: vcpkg (version, version-semver, version-date, version-string)
prerelease: In relaxed/semver schemes -<ident>(.<ident>)*; lower than the release; shorter numeric section list is lower than longer (1.0 < 1.0.0).
buildMetadata: +meta parsed, not compared (1.0.0+a and +b compare equal); not a stability signal.
postRelease: port-version (#N / port-version field) is a packaging post-release compared after the upstream version.
yankedDeprecated: None: ports are absent from the registry versions database; baselines set a floor. No yank or deprecation flag.
stableRule: Stable iff scheme is version or version-semver with no pre-release part, or version-date. version-string is unorderable and its stability cannot be inferred.
conventions: Four schemes per manifest, never compared across schemes; version-string only supports equality.
Resolution picks the LOWEST version satisfying all version>= constraints; overrides pin exact versions.
version-date is YYYY-MM-DD(.N)* with no calendar validation.
knownGaps: Docs disagree on whether relaxed version allows pre-release; source says yes.
Ported from C++, not executed.
2024-01-15 in relaxed version parses as a pre-release of 2024.

name: ZeroVer and unversioned refs
prerelease: As in SemVer when 0.y.z-<pre>; major stays 0.
buildMetadata: As SemVer: ignored, not a stability signal.
yankedDeprecated: Host ecosystem's mechanism.
stableRule: Same as the host scheme: stable iff no pre-release. 0.y.z is NOT unstable. HEAD, main, latest, nightly are refs, not versions.
conventions: Detection is by history: major==0 for about 95 percent of at least 10 stable releases over at least 2 years.
Caret on 0.x treats the minor as the breaking slot in Cargo, npm, Julia and pub.
knownGaps: No registry marks ZeroVer; purely heuristic.
Legacy shapes such as 0.9.8n need the host scheme's comparator.
